body: **2026-10-10-viola-revive** — added `revive` to the CLI verbs and made a passed revive enter the TUI passthrough boundary. Its exit-1 refusals take the fixed `unable:`/`hint:` form, a passed revive adds no SGR or line of its own, and the keystroke ban covers its start. This is the precedent for a restart-based switch that rides revive's start: the same boundary rows (tui-passthrough/entry, own-bytes, human-keystrokes) bind the switch, and any new way into the passthrough must be named on contract/tui-passthrough/entry.

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** — gave `revive` `--json` in both arms: each exit-1 refusal is one `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document with empty stderr, and the human pair stays byte-identical. A new switch verb's `--json` document and refusals extend this register (contract/revive-json-refusal/*, contract/start-json-refusal/document).

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — built the SGR spans: a word beside every span, and the colour decision reading NO_COLOR, TERM, COLORTERM and TTY, with no SGR under `--json` or a passthrough role. It also built the `--help` group labels over served verbs only, pinned by `help_is_the_grouped_verb_table` and `help_lists_only_served_verbs`. A new verb must take a row in one of board / traffic / wheel / handoff / setup and must print no SGR of its own in plain modes.

**2026-10-20-t06-58-31-wrap** — the founder ratified two things: `--help` rows over the served verbs only, and the board's cut width from `viola_pty::host_size()`. The served-verbs-only rule (contract/cli-help/served-verbs-only) is a standing founder decision that the switch verb's help row has to meet.

**2026-10-26-explicit-session-links** — the closest precedent for a new verb's a11y footprint. It added the `link`/`unlink` verb entity: one plain-ASCII result line in one write with no SGR, or one `{"v":1,"ok":…}` document. Refusals are exit 21 (strict-modes first, then a stopped instance, then server-verify) and wrapper invalid-params as an exit-20 fault with no hint. It also built the `handoff:` help row and the result lines pinned by literal, and fixed that printed names are the verb's parsed arguments, never read back from a reply or the log (decision/printed-names-are-parsed-arguments).

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** — the CLI frame verbs refuse a server that is not the recorded wrapper before any frame: exit 21 with the server-verify `hint:` last, or the `--json` document. The hint is pinned by literal, and the plugin and MCP against an impostor write no human-facing byte. If the switch reaches the live wrapper by a frame, it joins this list (contract/frame-verb-refusal/server-verify-failed, now eight verbs) and the literal-pin register.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — put the strict-modes check first. Frame verbs get exit 21 with the instance-state pair and run / revive start / verify get exit 1 with the home-state pair, before any log, with no line written; the plugin and MCP stay not-assertable. A switch verb (frame or start path) inherits decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write and must be added to its exit lists.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — set the `--json` failure discipline: one document, a literal exit, empty stderr, no ESC and no path or upstream text, witnessed by `cli_error_documents_hold_no_path_or_upstream_text`. It named the exit-2 exception (answer/send fixed line, no document), screened peer replies to code words (unknown exit 14, no hint), and added the error-writer census (`error_bodies_each_name_a_writer_and_a_witness_that_stand`, `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing`). A new verb's error bodies and any model/effort usage refusal must enter this census and the exit-2 exception if they follow its form.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — `revive --json` documents every refusal of the start it shares with `run`, and a `pump_child` error prints no document once the child has held the terminal. Exit 21's `--json` `detail` names its closed cause, and stale-heartbeat / already-live mark a start against a holder. It also built the exit-cause table `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`, `no_two_codes_share_a_hint` and `no_hint_names_release`. A new verb's codes and hints must take rows in this table and one hint per code, and none may name release.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — a refused socket directory is exit 1 at a start (revive's `socket-dir-refused` code, the fixed-message pair) and exit 21's sixth cause at the frame verbs, before any frame / snapshot / bind, with the directory left as found and the hint pinned by literal. A refused peer is dropped with no terminal byte and no wheel move. The switch's path (start or frame) inherits the matching socket-dir rows.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — narrowed to Linux only: the TUI boundary on openpty alone, the a11y cases on the one `ubuntu-latest` leg, and revive's `--json` codes ten (`batch-script-child` retired with its emitter). It also retired the macOS/Windows carve-outs for server-verify, socket-dir and strict-modes, and made the manual screen-reader pass Orca alone. The switch's cases run on ubuntu-latest only, and no OS arm is owed.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — CLI output discipline is checked through `std::process::Command` with every fixed string pinned by literal (trycmd/assert_cmd retired), and the outer-PTY driver is portable-pty `=0.9.0`, inherited and never re-pinned. The switch's result lines, hints and refusal layout must be pinned by literal on this harness (decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned, decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins).

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — the cli/tui a11y cases run as nextest cases inside the `coverage` suite under `gate --require coverage,doctest`. It bans a separate a11y driver or `suite` value outside `scripts/agent-run.sh run`, so the switch's a11y cases land in that suite with no harness of their own.

**2026-11-01-t02-46-44-wrap** — the founder kept the a11y tier at `Standard (1)` (decision/a11y-tier-standard): output-discipline and boundary assertions with no WCAG conformance claim. The switch is planned at this tier.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — fixed the closed non-editing list (focus, mouse, terminal replies), with every other byte taking the wheel, and set the wheel probe. Bears on the scope's open premise of whose wheel a switch needs: a switch typed into the live session must not be mistaken for human editing, and the human always wins.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — the readiness gate's bound falls on the driver, and a human key during the wait takes the wheel so the send is refused `human-typing` (exit 10) with nothing typed. This is the precedent for a switch that types into a live session: the human key wins, and the bound joins the driver-only time bounds.

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — a `/compact` send (a slash command typed into the session) has its own confirm window (40 s), a bound on the driver only, and fails with `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`. This is the precedent if the switch's channel is a command typed into the live session: its confirm window must be listed as a driver-only bound.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — made the dialog hold configurable (`dialog_hold_s` 60–3600). The hold bounds the driver, and any human key hands a held dialog back at once (decision/dialog-hold-bounds-the-driver). Bears on the scope's premise of what a switch does to a session holding a dialog.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — retired exit 11 (`budget-paused`), never to be reused, with an older wrapper's word reading `unknown` (14). It also dropped the budget pause from the time-bound lists. A trap for the switch's exit codes: 11 must not be reused.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** — the start's trust step reports its word in one `trust-record` diagnostics line, never on the terminal or as a refusal, and the start's Claude config lock wait joins the time bounds, falling on viola's own start. A restart-based switch rides this start, and any settings-adjacent write must stay off the terminal (decision/run-diagnostics-off-terminal).

**2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically** — a keyed start's automatic-verify window is the one exception to the never-blocked keystroke and zero-viola-bytes promises, holding from the child's start. Ratified at 2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap. A restarted session carries the same exception and no new one.

**2026-11-22-paste-write-bounded** — human keystrokes wait at most behind the paste's in-flight chunk and closing marker (contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes, decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked). This binds any switch that writes into the live session.

**2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap** — reworded own-bytes, zero-viola-bytes, wheel-ignores-terminal-events and portable-pty-outer-pty-driver for the automatic-verify exception. It added paste write to both time-bound lists and the row decision/compiled-shapes-over-signatures. These are the standing forms of rows the switch's boundary rests on.

**2026-11-22-epoch-4-cleanup** — the two time-bound lists are full at their bound, so a new time bound lands as a row of its own (decision/start-verify-stop-grace-off-the-human). Any bound the switch adds (a restart wait, a confirm window) follows this ruling.

**2026-11-24-viola-up** — the closest recent precedents for a new verb. It added contract/viola-up-output/instance-line for a new verb's output line and put `up` on exit 21's list. It reworded the two time-bound lists to «Eight» (state provisional) and gave three new bounds rows of their own (open live wait, window wait, hyprctl read). A new switch verb follows these: an output-line row, its own exit-cause wording, and any new bound in a row of its own.

**2026-11-24-viola-focus** — a non-frame verb joined exit 21 (contract/cli-exit-codes/21) and the strict-modes exit-21 list, refused before any compositor read (provisional, delegate). Precedent for naming the switch verb in those rows if it refuses there.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** — adopt's start was added to every start row: home-strict-modes, socket-dir, strict-modes-before-any-write, json-fault internal-error silence, fixed-message form, the unable-line exceptions, start-json-refusal/document, tui-passthrough/entry, log-identity/process, and agents-read fail-open. A switch that restarts through the shared start must be named the same way in each row.

**2026-11-23-viola-open-2** — `viola open`'s refused word after `--` became an exit-2 fixed stderr line with no document that echoes none of the refused words (contract/cli-exit-codes/2, decision/json-one-document-no-hint, contract/cli-refusal/json). This is the precedent for an unusable model/effort word: either it joins the exit-2 exception or it takes a hint-free document.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — revive's single `claude agents --json` read (5 s kill) fails open, a bound on viola's own child, never the human. A restart-based switch through revive's preflight inherits this read and its fail-open rule.

**2026-11-21-mcp-calls-bounded** — added the MCP call deadline (55 s) as a driver-only bound and `call-deadline` as an MCP-only unreachable cause, with the CLI's exit-21 causes staying six. If a fork brings in an MCP tool for the switch, it inherits this deadline. On the CLI-only arm, no exit-21 cause is added.

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** — the rendered TUI screen is parsed only for compiled signatures, and later wraps narrowed this to compiled shapes, with the prompt row read only for its opening char. If the switch's channel is a command typed into the live session, confirming it may not read screen text beyond these signatures (decision/no-screen-content-parsing).

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — a second live reading of the takeover clause, supplemental and never gating (decision/live-readings-never-gate). This phase runs nothing live, so the switch's wheel claims rest on outer-PTY cases alone.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — added the after-feed-panic boundary: `send` refused `input-not-ready` while a human key still reaches the child, and no viola literal on the outer terminal. A switch typed through the send path meets the same readiness refusal.

**2026-11-22-lineage-registry** — the terminal structural equivalents gained the `-- LINKS --` separator and the NAME tree indent. If the switch surfaces the new pair on the board, it must fit these equivalents and the static, linear output.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — the CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) report inside the CI `coverage` suite (decision/cli-invariants-pass-in-ci). The switch's output-discipline cases are gated there.

Builds a new viola CLI verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session (a named instance) to a given model and effort.
It records the new pair so a later resume (viola revive, viola up) replays the new pair, not the one named at launch.
It has no side effect on the user's own settings: it writes nothing to the user's or a project's claude settings and does not use the CLI's own model command as its channel.
It adds the verb's argument surface, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, --json document, an events-log record of the switch and its process-log lines, each beside the existing tables.
Nothing live: its proof is by tests only, with no real session read, switched or resumed and no read of the operator's real home.
The new verb on the viola --help surface: its usage line and its row among the served verbs, with its argument surface (instance name, model, effort).

The closed sets the verb's arguments are checked against: model words and effort levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max); a word outside them is a usage error with CLI exit code 2 and a refusal on stderr.

The verb's refusals on stderr: the unable line with its kebab-case reason code beside it, the detail, and the hint line ending every refusal, one hint per code, faults carrying no hint, no stack trace or bare status as error text.
The verb's --json output: one document, success or failure, with no hint and clean failure documents, beside the existing --json refusal and fault documents.

The verb's exit codes and exit causes beside the CLI exit code catalogue (2, 10, 11, 13, 14, 20, 21 as they apply), including exit 21 when the named instance is unreachable and its instance-unreachable detail (instance-dead, endpoint-lost, call-deadline, unwrapped-name, socket-dir-refused, strict-modes-failed, server-verify-failed).

Reaching a named instance from a CLI verb: socket-directory and strict-modes refusals before any frame or write, server-verify-failed when the peer is not the recorded wrapper, peer replies screened to code words, unlisted code words left visible.

The verb's human result line: static, linear, written in one write, no spinner, no SGR off a colour-capable terminal and never on a failure word, C0/C1 control characters escaped, the printed instance name being the parsed argument.

The recorded launch pair a resume replays: after a switch, viola revive and viola up start the session on the new model and effort, not the launch pair, including the revive --model / --effort override path and the start refusals of a resumed start (already-live, stale-heartbeat, session-live and the other revive refusals).

If the switch rides a restart of the session (end and resume), the TUI passthrough of the resumed child holds: zero viola bytes on the human's terminal, run diagnostics never on the terminal, the terminal belonging to the child.

A switch against a session mid-turn, holding a dialog, or while the human types: human keystrokes are never blocked, a human key takes the wheel, a driver write is refused while the human types, and the dialog hold bounds the driver, not the human.
Time bounds the switch may wait on (a reply deadline, a resume's live wait, a stop grace) fall on the driver only, never on the human, and none is a harsh timeout without warning.
The events-log record of the switch: a new event line kind with its fields, beside the existing event line kinds.
The verb's process-log lines: log identity tags (process, service_name), and the lines kept off the terminal.

The settings boundary as a check: the switch writes nothing to the user's or project's claude settings, proved by tests against a fixture home, never the operator's real one, with no live reading gating the proof.
The verb's new fixed CLI strings (result line, refusal copy, hints) come from design copy, are pinned by literal in tests, and name no release.

body_fields.convention: each new a11y assertion runs inside the existing test suites under nextest in the GitHub Actions push/PR workflow, as a nextest failure, with no skips, no retries and no a11y artifact of its own
each new fixed CLI string, caption, refusal and hint is pinned by its literal in a test, and refusal layout is held by literal pins
each new refusal is a word, a detail and a hint, its reason code beside the unable word, one hint per code, faults with no hint
each new CLI output line is linear and static, escapes control bytes, carries no SGR off a terminal and none beside a failure word
each new log line carries the log identity tags and never reaches the human's terminal
each new boundary test is sequenced on records, never inspects claude content, and no live reading gates it

body: The viola list board's rows, captions, colour, stale-row dim, amber DIALOG word and NAME truncation: the chunk prints no board.
The console's keyboard reach of the switch and keyboard navigation of a fleet console: owned by another route entry, not this chunk.
Manual Orca and keyboard passes and the screen-reader targets and setups for the cli and tui: supplemental, gating nothing this chunk builds.
Other verbs' own outputs: viola link and unlink, viola plugin install, viola verify and its interrupted pair, viola wait, viola open's live wait and the compositor and window wait bounds.
Web, graphical, touch, rendered-page and internationalization absences, and the N/A structured-violation, WCAG mapping, contrast and focus-management harness areas.
The claude agents read and the client euid refusal test strategy: the switch neither lists agents nor serves a hook client.

**2026-11-23-model-and-effort-at-launch** (Established Decisions: 2 rows) — `~ decision/revive-resumes-in-place` narrowed to "replays no launch spec but the recorded model and effort", and `+ decision/launch-pair-handed-not-verified`: every start hands the pair on argv and it is never read back or verified. This is the base the switch builds on. A switch that "takes effect for the next turn" cannot be verified by the same rule, and a recorded new pair is exactly what revive replays.

Adds a new viola CLI verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session, a named instance, to a given model and effort.
The verb records the new pair, so a later resume through revive or up replays the new pair and not the one named at launch.
It has no side effect on the user's own settings: it writes nothing to the user's claude home or to a project's settings files, and it never uses the CLI's own model command as its channel.
It adds the verb's arguments, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, --json document, the events-log record of the switch and its process-log lines, each placed beside the existing tables.
Nothing runs live: no real session is read, switched, ended or resumed, and no real claude home is read.

body: The new verb is a CLI subcommand on a named instance, added beside the CLI verbs table and the command names. It follows the CLI flag and subcommand style, the clap parser, and the rule that new capabilities arrive as subcommands or channel verbs.

The verb's arguments are the model and the effort. They are checked against the closed model-word format and the closed effort set (low, medium, high, xhigh, max). The compiled default launch pair and the configured default model and effort stay what they are.

The switch records the new pair as the pair a resume replays: the launch event kind and its data, the wrapper's launch append, and the instance snapshot's launch field. Revive and up then hand the recorded pair on the child's command line, which the launch-pair flags passed to the child carry.

The events-log record of the switch is a normalised event kind. It is added only in viola-core, follows the event line's shape, source and data, and is appended as one write per line under the versioned, tolerant own-format rules. The snapshot replay still recovers the pair from log-derived fields.

No side effect on the user's settings: the switch writes no settings layer, passes no --settings at start, leaves the global statusline config untouched and writes no user-scope model key. The CLI's own model command, which writes that key, is not the channel.

A switch that restarts the session rides the revive start path. That path resumes in place, refuses a session a live claude holds, never starts over a live or stale instance, refuses a held name and resolves the child program itself. It ends the running session and resumes it, which shows in session liveness and in the session-end and session-start records.

The ways a running session's model or effort can change, and which of them writes where, are read only from the capability ledger's recorded rows. The ledger is the single gate for CLI behaviour, and local commands are classified by it. Anything the ledger does not hold is unmeasured and is not relied on.

A switch asked for mid-turn, mid-send or while a dialog is held must obey the wheel and the send gate. The human always wins the wheel, a send mid-turn is refused and never queued, and there is at most one pending dialog with a dialog hold per instance.

If the verb reaches the running wrapper over the channel, it is a frame-writing client. It runs the strict-modes check, the socket-directory check and the server-identity check in their one order before the first frame. It reports unreachable causes through exit 21 and its documents. A new channel method follows the channel methods table and the protocol-version bump rule.

The verb's exit codes are drawn from the CLI exit codes table and the exit-cause catalogue, and a retired code is never reused. Its refusals come from the closed set of refusal details, only the first refusal is returned, and the closed words use kebab-case wire values.

The verb's output prints human text by default and a --json document on request, in declared key order with snake_case field names and absent optional fields omitted. Errors use the CLI --json error document and the human error line, both sanitised. Hint lines are short-lived CLI stderr lines.

The verb's process-log lines are codes-only lines in its role's home-level diagnostics file (the cli role file). They are emitted only through the one event emitter, and error context chains reach only the detail file.
The board's model and effort fields of a list item show the recorded pair, so after a switch they read the new pair.
Claude-specific flag literals and pair shapes stay in the claude agent crate, which does no file I/O. The root bin consumes only normalised events.

body_fields.convention: Every new test runs against the fake agent in its own isolated viola home. No live claude runs in CI, and real-CLI probes run only locally.
Every new error variant joins its crate's one thiserror enum, and its message interpolates nothing. anyhow appears only at the root bin edge.
Every new module joins the module tree, with no orphan modules, no print or dbg macros and no tracing level macros. It passes fmt and clippy with warnings denied.
Every new test respects the coverage floors, zero panic lines in end-to-end runs, and insta snapshots in check mode only.
Every new test seam or knob uses the fake-agent test seam variables or the AGENT_RUN_ harness prefix. These are never a configuration channel the product reads.

Adds a new flat viola CLI verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session (a named instance) to a given model and effort.
It records the new model and effort pair so that a later resume through viola revive or viola up replays the new pair, not the one named at launch.
The verb has no side effect on the user's own settings and does not use the CLI's own model command as its channel.
It adds the verb's argument surface, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, --json document, events-log record and process-log lines beside the existing CLI verb, exit-cause, closed-detail and event-kind tables.
The register of CLI command names gains one new verb name, a flat top-level verb beside run, revive, up, open, send and the rest, never a nested subcommand group.

The new verb's human output: a result line on stderr confirming the switch with its context (the instance name and the new model and effort), in the fixed phraseology vocabulary, ASCII-only, with no check-mark or emoji prefix.
Nothing announces success before confirmation: the verb reports the switch only once it is confirmed to have taken effect for the instance, never optimistically.
The new verb's --json result is one document on stdout, success or refusal, with clean failure documents and no hint line under --json.

The new verb's exit codes join the CLI exit-code table: 0 on a confirmed switch, 1 for its own refusals with closed refusal codes, 2 for a usage error such as an unknown model word or effort level, and 21 with its existing causes where the instance cannot be reached.

Instance-unreachable refusals of the new verb use the existing exit-21 cause catalogue (unwrapped-name, instance-dead, endpoint-lost, socket-dir-refused, strict-modes-failed, server-verify-failed) and their one hint per cause, in human and --json form.
Unwrapped sessions are never a target: a name that is no viola-wrapped instance is refused as unwrapped-name, never switched.

Refusal lines of the new verb follow the CLI refusal-line form (an unable line and at most one hint line on stderr), hints in human mode only, no hint for faults or unknown, no hint naming viola release, hints never quoting text, and no internals, paths or pids in errors or hints.

Adds a viola verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session, a named instance, to a given model and effort.
It records the new pair so that a later resume (revive, up) replays the new pair, not the one named at launch.
The verb has no side effect on the user's own settings: it writes nothing to the user's claude home or a project's settings, and does not use the CLI's own model command as its channel.
It adds the verb's argument surface, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, --json document, the events-log record of the switch and its process-log lines, each beside the existing tables.

body: A new short-lived CLI verb, the switch, addressed to a named instance: its arguments, its closed model and effort words, its exit codes and the closed detail code each exit cause carries, beside the existing CLI verb and exit-cause tables.
The switch verb's human output: lines on stdout for success, and on a refusal the fixed unable and hint pair on stderr, interpolating no path, pid or content.

The switch verb's --json document, for success and for each refusal, including an internal-error document and an instance-unreachable document with its one cause word when the named instance is dead, lost or not wrapped.

The switch verb's CLI process-log file and lines: process-start and process-exit in the cli role file, written only under a parsed instance name, with a distinct closed detail code per exit cause; the instance is taken from the name, never the working directory.
A new events-log record of the switch carrying the new model and effort pair, in the event line shape, emitted deterministically; the event payload stays out of the process logs.
The recorded pair a resume replays: the launch line and the snapshot's launch field, read by product readers through replay, so that revive and up start the resumed child on the last recorded pair.

Where the switch restarts the session through the revive start path with a new pair, that path's rules bind it: revive start logs as run, the revive preflight order and its cwd-missing, no-session and session-live details, the run start process log and spans, and the claude-child process-start line.
Model and effort words are closed sets validated before any action: a word outside them is refused with a closed detail code, never echoed back in a log line or error message.
Any new log field naming the model or effort is an additive, allow-listed, closed-enum field in the diagnostics line schema; the field allow-list is default-deny and existing field names stay frozen.
No side effect on settings: the verb writes no user-scope or project settings file; the child settings argument and the stripped CLAUDE environment values passed on a restart are never logged.

The home strict-modes and home-tree checks run before the verb's log opens; a refusal before the log opens writes no line, and socket-directory and server-verification refusals keep their fixed codes if the verb reaches the instance's endpoint.

If the switch reaches the live wrapper over the channel, its channel-request and channel-response lines carry no params or result bodies, correlate by corr and conn, and the wrapper's refusal reasons stay closed detail words.
The verb's dispatch gets one manual span with a static name, skipping all arguments, with an explicit field allow-list and no endpoint, path or env values; spans are not serialized.

Errors in the verb are typed with fixed Display messages, anyhow only at the dispatch edge, the full error chain only in the detail file; serde errors become the fixed internal-error message; a cli panic follows the cli panic outcome.
Every line the verb writes goes through the obs_event macro with a closed event value; no print macros and no raw tracing macros in its code paths; log level never from the environment.

The verb's tests run against the fake agent only, never the real CLI and never the operator's real home or board; integration-test homes stay under the scanned test root and their emitted lines pass the schema conformance and zero-panics gates.
Session ids the switch reads or passes to resume are typed fields, never logged in content or interpolated into messages.

body_fields.convention: each new log line or event is emitted through the obs_event macro with a closed event value, corr where correlated, and carries no content, path or secret
each new log field is additive to the diagnostics line schema, named under the additive naming rule and admitted to the default-deny allow-list
each new span declares a static name, skips all arguments and lists its allowed fields explicitly
each new integration or end-to-end test keeps its home under the scanned test root until the gates run, and its emitted lines are schema-checked and counted by the panic gate
each new fixture or test input is synthetic, never recorded from a real session or the operator's real home

Builds a new viola CLI verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session, named by its instance name, to a given model and effort word.
It records the new launch pair so a later resume (revive, up) replays the new pair, not the one named at launch.
It has no side effect on the user's settings: it writes nothing under the Claude home or a project's Claude settings, and it does not use the CLI's own model command as its channel.
It adds the verb's argument surface, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, --json document, an events-log record of the switch and its process-log lines beside the existing tables.
At P3 it re-reads how revive's pair override, the recorded launch pair, the closed model and effort sets, the wheel and the send gate stand. Nothing live runs in this phase.

body: The new verb's input: the instance name goes through the viola name check and validated name type, and the model and effort words are checked against their closed sets (core model-word check, the adapter's effort-word check) before any state is read, any frame is sent or any child is spawned; a bad word is refused whole.
No write under the Claude home or into a project's Claude settings: the switch must leave the user's settings byte-identical, so its channel cannot be the CLI's model command or any settings write.

The recorded launch pair: the new pair is recorded where a resume replays it (the snapshot's launch record and the event log's launch lines), kept to the snapshot and the event log only, handed to the claude child as argv elements, authenticating nothing, and shown on the board only when it re-parses.

State writes the switch makes: only the instance's own wrapper writes its snapshot; event-log appends heal a torn last line and readers tolerate torn lines; files are replaced through the one shared replace helper with owner-only modes set before any byte.

The strict-modes check on the viola home and state tree comes before the verb reads the snapshot or any trusted state, before any log opens, and a strict-modes refusal leaves no trace; the new verb needs its own strict-modes refusal output beside the other verbs'.

If the switch reaches the wrapper over the local channel: the client's check order (instance check first, socket-directory check, server verified before any frame, peer euid check), closed channel types, the frame cap, and a new channel method needing its process-log entry and its params, errors and channel-response detail rows.

If the switch is typed into the live session: the send gate's rules — text typed as one bracketed paste, control-character and empty-text refusals, the wrapper re-checking text authoritatively — and human typing taking the wheel; what a switch mid-turn or under a held dialog does is measured at P3.

If the switch restarts the session through the revive path: revive's checks before use (strict modes, socket-directory refusal, start collision check already-live / stale-heartbeat, pinned binary re-hash), the recorded cwd used only to spawn, and the child's environment with parent identity variables and inherited CLAUDE credentials stripped.
Targets: the verb acts only on a viola-wrapped instance it can reach; an unwrapped session or agent name is never a target, and the verb acts on no process viola did not start.

The verb's exit codes and refusal words beside the CLI exit-code table and the instance-unreachable details and causes (exit 21, its --json document and stderr hints), the --json error documents including internal-error, with no paths, pids or ids in any refusal.
The verb's human and --json output: fixed error display messages that interpolate nothing and quote no upstream text, C0/C1 controls escaped in human output, full error detail only in diagnostics.
The events-log record of the switch: its kind and data beside the existing event kinds, holding the closed model and effort words and no user content, CLAUDE value or path.
The verb's process-log lines: closed details only, never logging CLAUDE values or user content, stderr honouring the never-log floor.
No new flag, config value or environment variable the verb brings may switch off a control; configuration and environment are not a channel for the pair.
If a fork settles an MCP tool for the switch: the MCP tool list and tool-input contracts, schema-checked raw arguments, the frame-tool refusals and isError structuredContent codes.

The proof of no settings side effect: tests prove the user's settings byte-identical against a test-owned home and the fake agent, never the real Claude home, real claude CLI or a real session; the real CLI run on the pair is carried elsewhere.

body_fields.convention: each new test uses its own viola home and its own Claude home, never the user's, and CI runs no real claude CLI and holds no secrets
each new environment read, seam, listener or channel method gets its process-log entry
each new error or refusal output uses a fixed message and closed code words, with no paths, type names or upstream text
each new recorded fixture is scrubbed, reviewed and under the hygiene walk, or refused whole
each new test seam lives only under the fake-agent feature and is compiled out of release
each new validated input goes through the shared validators in the core crate

body: A new CLI verb in the verb table: it takes a named wrapped instance and a model and effort, switches that session to the pair for its next turn, and returns one outcome per run.

The recorded pair a resume replays: the switch leaves a record (a launch model and effort line in the instance event log, and the launch field the snapshot holds and replay recovers) so that revive and up start the child on the new pair. Snapshot readers go through read-or-replay, and the snapshot and its log keep their single writers.

No side effect on the user's settings: the verb writes nothing to the user's claude home files or to a project's claude settings files. Tests prove those files are byte-identical before and after a switch, in a test-owned user home.
The agent CLI's own model command is not the switch channel, because it writes the user-scope model key. The verb never types or sends it into the session.

Closed words of the argument surface: model words are checked by the core model-word check and effort words by the agent's closed effort set. The compiled default pair is the fallback. Any new closed word is changed only by a recorded decision.
The verb's exit codes and exit-cause catalogue entries: each cause has its own hint, and no hint suggests release to a driver.

Human-mode output lines of the verb: they are pinned as literals, they escape control characters, they carry no SGR or other escape bytes without a terminal, and their error lines hold no path or upstream text.
The verb's --json output: one JSON document on stdout per run, with an ok document and a failure document (refusal, instance-unreachable, internal-error) shaped like the other verbs' documents.

The events-log record of a switch: a new event kind in the events catalogue, written as one complete event line with the standard keys and ts. Readers that do not know the kind count it and skip it; they never fail on it.

The verb's process-log lines: structured JSON lines through the one tracing install, codes only with detail kept apart, corr where always defined, closed details added to the observability plan's closed-detail list, and no secrets, prompt text or session names.

Indirect, through the instance it targets: the verb checks the instance first, reaches only the recorded wrapper at the endpoint read from the snapshot, and verifies the server's identity, the socket directory and strict modes before any frame or read. Its unreachable outcomes take the existing instance-unreachable causes and exit 21.
Indirect: an unwrapped agent-list row name is never a switch target, and a name that is not a running wrapped instance is refused with the existing cause words.

Indirect, through the existing start path: if the switch restarts the session on the new pair, it goes through revive's preflight order and its refusal codes (session-live, already-live, stale-heartbeat and the rest). A start appends exactly one launch model and effort record, and the pair reaches the claude child's argv. Tests read that argv from the live child's cmdline.

Indirect, through the claude child: a restarted child keeps the child environment strip, so nothing of viola's or of the user's CLAUDE* identity leaks into it. The child runs under the test-owned user home in tests.

The verb's tests run against the fake agent standing in for claude, as a subprocess, in a fresh test-owned home. They never touch the real claude CLI, the host's claude sessions, or the operator's real claude home or board.
Error payloads of the verb are sanitized: thiserror messages interpolate nothing, and every new error writer is named.
